mainTopic: Laws of taking, holding and smelling the ארבעה מינים, and where and why the לולב is waved
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a proof from a משנה in מסכת פרה: tipping ashes into water through a tube still counts, so לקיחה על ידי דבר אחר שמה לקיחה. This supports רבא, who allows holding the לולב through a cloth. Next, רבה gives a series of practical rulings about the ארבעה מינים. Twice he warns that loose leaves inside the bundle may be a חציצה, and twice רבא answers that מין במינו אינו חוצץ. רבה also rules on smelling: one may not smell a הדס set aside for the מצוה, but one may smell the אתרוג, and on שבת an attached הדס may be smelled while an attached אתרוג may not. He then rules that the לולב goes in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left. רבי זריקא explains that the ברכה names only the לולב because the palm is the tallest of the species. A new משנה follows, listing where in הלל the לולב is waved. בית הלל and בית שמאי disagree about הצליחה נא, and רבי עקיבא's report supports בית הלל. The גמרא explains how waving is done and gives two reasons for it: praising the Owner of the world, or holding back harmful winds and dews. A final lesson from this begins here and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: if he poured the ashes in himself, it is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה of the tube that fell into the water: if the person himself tipped it in, the mixture is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he himself tipped it in, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה in מסכת פרה closely and draws an inference from it. The משנה says that if the tube of ashes fell into the water by accident, the mixture is פסול. So if the person tipped the ashes in himself, the mixture must be כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full proof belongs to רבא, who holds that taking through another object counts as taking. In the case of the משנה, the person never touches the ashes with his hand; he only tips the tube. Even so, his action is valid, and this is the first building block of the proof.

phrases.english: By implication, if he himself made it fall in, it is valid.
phrases.notes: We learn this from the משנה in פרה, which says a tube that fell into the water is פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's proof from the משנה of the tube (from the end of the previous section).
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that לקיחה על ידי דבר אחר שמה לקיחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת פרה about a tube of ashes that fell into the water

steps.title: Why should it be valid if the Torah requires taking and placing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why tipping the tube should work, since the Torah says 'they shall take' and 'he shall place'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? The Torah says 'they shall take' and 'he shall place'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question to set up the punchline of the proof. If the Torah demands a real act of 'taking' and 'placing', why does tipping a tube count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in במדבר י״ט requires a deliberate act of taking the ashes and placing them with the water. Tipping a tube does not look like taking with the hand. The question shows that there must be a reason the act still works, and the next step gives that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, i.e. the תורה

phrases.english: Why?
The Merciful One said 'and they shall take' and 'and he shall place'!
phrases.notes: These words make it sound like someone really has to take it with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the inference just drawn, in order to sharpen the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that tipping the tube into the water is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires taking and placing, and tipping a tube is not direct taking.

steps.title: Conclusion: taking through another object counts as taking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the act must count as taking even though it was done through a tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that taking by means of another object is called taking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רבא's proof. The only way to explain the משנה is that taking through an object, like a tube, is still a valid לקיחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule applies to the לולב: holding it through a cloth would still count as taking it. This supports רבא against רבה, who said a cloth is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: taking by means of another object

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, לקיחה על ידי דבר אחר שמה לקיחה. Taking something through an intermediate object, such as a tube or a cloth, still counts as taking it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle decides whether one may hold the לולב with a cloth or glove and still be יוצא.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so? Learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: לְקִיחָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר — שְׁמָהּ לְקִיחָה.
phrases.english: Taking by means of another object is called taking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 and closes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that taking through another object counts as taking
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implication of the משנה in פרה together with the פסוק 'ולקחו… ונתן'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לקיחה על ידי דבר אחר שמה לקיחה

steps.title: רבה: do not push the לולב into the bundle after it is tied
steps.stepSummary: רבה warns against sticking the לולב into an already-tied bundle of הדסים and ערבות, because leaves may fall off and become a חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: A person should not stick the לולב into the bundle, because perhaps leaves will fall off and become a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new practical warning about putting the bundle together. Do not tie the הדסים and ערבות first and then push the לולב in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing the לולב in may knock leaves off, and those loose leaves could sit between the species. A barrier like that might stop the species from counting as one bundle taken together. רבה treats such leaves as a חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: the bundle of species (here: the binding)

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
A person should not stick the lulav into the bundle,
because perhaps leaves will fall off
and it will be an interposition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: לָא לִדוּץ אִינִישׁ לוּלַבָּא בְּהוֹשַׁעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement of רבה on a related topic: the proper way to take the ארבעה מינים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not insert the לולב into a tied bundle, because fallen leaves may form a חציצה.

steps.title: רבא: the same species is not a barrier
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees, holding that leaves of the same species do not form a barrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: One species with its own kind does not interpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רבה's concern. Leaves from these plants are not a foreign barrier, so they do not create a חציצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חציצה is normally a foreign substance that separates two things. Leaves that come from the species themselves count as part of the bundle, not as something separating it. So, according to רבא, there is no reason to avoid pushing the לולב in.

keyTerms.meaning: a species with its own kind

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A species with its own kind does not interpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: מִין בְּמִינוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבה's reasoning in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The concern of חציצה from fallen leaves
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Material of the same species is not considered a barrier.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (בה with a ה) and רבא (בא with an א). They are two different אמוראים who argue here.

steps.title: רבה: do not trim the לולב while it is in the bundle
steps.stepSummary: רבה warns against cutting the לולב while it is inside the binding, because leftover strips may become a חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: A person should not cut the לולב while it is in the bundle, because strips of palm leaf will remain and be a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second, similar warning. Do not trim the לולב after it is already tied into the bundle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting it in place may leave small strips of palm leaf caught between the species. רבה again treats these leftovers as a possible חציצה.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
A person should not cut the lulav while in the bundle,
because palm strips remain and it will be an interposition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: לָא לִיגּוֹז אִינִישׁ לוּלַבָּא בְּהוֹשַׁעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement of רבה built on the same concern of חציצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not cut the לולב while it is in the bundle, because leftover strips may form a חציצה.

steps.title: רבא again: the same species is not a barrier
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the same answer: material of the same species does not interpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: One species with its own kind does not interpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבא's answer, now aimed at רבה's second warning. Leftover palm strips are not a barrier either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the strips come from the לולב itself, so they are clearly the same species. רבא's single principle answers both of רבה's concerns.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה worries that loose leaves or strips inside the bundle are a חציצה. רבא answers that מין במינו אינו חוצץ, so the same species never counts as a barrier.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A species with its own kind does not interpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: מִין בְּמִינוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבה's reasoning in step 6, using the same principle as step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The concern of חציצה from leftover palm strips
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Strips from the לולב itself are the same species and do not interpose.

steps.title: רבה: smelling the מצוה הדס is forbidden, smelling the מצוה אתרוג is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that one may not smell a הדס set aside for the מצוה, but one may smell an אתרוג set aside for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: It is forbidden to smell a הדס of the מצוה, and it is permitted to smell an אתרוג of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new ruling about enjoying the smell of the species. He treats the הדס and the אתרוג differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are set aside for the מצוה, yet one may be smelled and the other may not. This difference begs for an explanation, which the גמרא asks for next.

keyTerms.meaning: a myrtle set aside for the מצוה

phrases.english: And Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַס שֶׁל מִצְוָה — אָסוּר לְהָרִיחַ בּוֹ,
phrases.english: A myrtle of the מצוה: it is forbidden to smell it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶתְרוֹג שֶׁל מִצְוָה — מוּתָּר לְהָרִיחַ בּוֹ.
phrases.english: an etrog of the מצוה: it is permitted to smell it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: הֲדַס שֶׁל מִצְוָה אָסוּר לְהָרִיחַ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: enjoying items set aside for the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smelling the מצוה הדס is forbidden, and smelling the מצוה אתרוג is permitted.

steps.title: What is the reason for the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבה treats the הדס and the אתרוג differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבה's ruling. This short line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items are designated for the מצוה, so we would expect the same rule for both. The question asks what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why smelling the הדס is forbidden but smelling the אתרוג is allowed

steps.title: Each species is set aside only from its main use
steps.stepSummary: The הדס exists for its smell, so setting it aside removes smelling. The אתרוג exists for eating, so setting it aside removes only eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: A הדס stands for its fragrance, so when one sets it aside, he sets it aside from fragrance. An אתרוג stands for eating, so when one sets it aside, he sets it aside from eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that setting something aside for a מצוה blocks only its main use. For a הדס, the main use is smelling. For an אתרוג, the main use is eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person designates an item for the מצוה (הקצאה), he gives up the main benefit the item is normally used for. Smell is the whole point of a הדס, so smelling it is forbidden. Smell is only a side benefit of an אתרוג, so smelling it stays permitted; only eating it is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Designating a מצוה object (הקצאה) forbids only its main normal use. A הדס is used for smelling, so smelling it is forbidden. An אתרוג is used for eating, so eating it is forbidden but smelling it is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that one may smell the אתרוג of the מצוה but not the הדס during סוכות.

phrases.english: A myrtle, which stands for fragrance,
when he set it aside, he set it aside from fragrance.
An etrog, which stands for eating,
when he set it aside, he set it aside from eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Setting an item aside forbids only its main purpose: smell for the הדס and eating for the אתרוג.

steps.title: Smelling an attached הדס versus an attached אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that one may smell a הדס still attached to its bush, but not an אתרוג still hanging on its tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: a הדס that is still attached to the ground may be smelled. An אתרוג that is still attached to the tree may not be smelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new ruling about smelling plants that are still growing, which matters on שבת, when cutting a plant is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smelling itself is not the problem. The question is whether smelling might lead a person to pick the plant. רבה treats the הדס and the אתרוג differently, and the reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: While still attached to the ground or tree

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different case from Step 8. There, the הדס and אתרוג had already been cut and set aside for the מצוה. Here, they are still growing, and the concern is that a person might pick them on שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
A myrtle while it is attached (to the ground)
it is permitted to smell it,
an etrog while it is attached (to the tree)
it is forbidden to smell it.
phrases.notes: The concern applies on שבת, when picking is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling of רבה in the same series about the ארבעה מינים and smelling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An attached הדס may be smelled; an attached אתרוג may not.

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind the difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the attached הדס and the attached אתרוג are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבה's ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both plants smell good, so a reader would expect them to follow the same rule. The question looks for the factor that separates them.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why smelling an attached הדס is allowed but smelling an attached אתרוג is forbidden.

steps.title: Smelling does not lead to cutting a הדס, but it may lead to picking an אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: A הדס exists for its smell, so smelling it fully satisfies the person. An אתרוג exists for eating, so smelling it may tempt the person to pick and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A הדס is meant for smelling. If you allow him to smell it, he will not come to cut it. An אתרוג is meant for eating. If you allow him to smell it, he will come to pick it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the rule depends on what each plant is mainly used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a הדס, smelling is the main enjoyment, so once he smells it he is done and has no reason to cut it. With an אתרוג, the smell makes him want to eat it, so there is a real risk he will pick it on שבת. This is a protective rule to keep him away from the forbidden act of picking.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands for / exists for (its main purpose)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule follows the plant's main use. Smelling a plant that is meant to be eaten can lead to picking it, so it is forbidden while attached.

phrases.english: A myrtle, which exists for smelling,
if you permit him (to smell it),
he will not come to cut it.
An etrog, which exists for eating,
if you permit him (to smell it),
he will come to pick it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The main purpose of each plant decides whether smelling is likely to lead to picking.

steps.title: לולב in the right hand, אתרוג in the left
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that the לולב bundle is held in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: the לולב goes in the right hand, and the אתרוג in the left.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new practical ruling about which hand holds which item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word לולב means the whole bundle: the לולב, the הדסים and the ערבות. The right hand is the more important hand, so the question is which item deserves it.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
The lulav (bundle) goes in the right hand,
and the etrog in the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in רבה's series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לולב bundle is held in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה followed today.

steps.title: Asking why the לולב gets the right hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the לולב gets the more important hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבה's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought the אתרוג, the most beautiful of the four, deserves the right hand. The question looks for the principle that decides it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the לולב goes in the right hand and the אתרוג in the left.

steps.title: Three מצוות outrank one
steps.stepSummary: The bundle holds three of the מינים, while the אתרוג is only one, so the bundle gets the more important right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are three מצוות, and this is one מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the right hand goes to the side holding more מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב, הדס and ערבה are three separate מינים, each its own מצוה. The אתרוג is just one. Honor goes to the greater number of מצוות.

phrases.english: These are three מצוות,
and this is one מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The right hand goes to the item that holds more מצוות.

steps.title: Why the ברכה names only the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זריקא why the ברכה says only על נטילת לולב and does not mention the other three מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זריקא: What is the reason that we bless only 'על נטילת לולב'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes up: the ברכה is said over four מינים, yet it names only the לולב. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 counted the bound species as three separate מצוות, so it seems odd that the ברכה gives the לולב all the credit. רבי ירמיה wants to know what makes the לולב the representative of the whole group.

keyTerms.meaning: About taking the לולב (the wording of the ברכה)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זְרִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zerika:
What is the reason we do not bless
except 'about taking the lulav'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related question about the ארבעה מינים, prompted by the theme of which species is more important.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברכה wording mentions only the לולב.

steps.title: Because the לולב is the highest
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא answers that the לולב is the tallest item in the bundle, so the ברכה is named after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is the highest of them all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זריקא gives a first answer: the לולב sticks up above everything else, so it stands for the whole group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The most visible item gives its name to the bundle. The next step challenges whether physical height alone is a good enough reason.

phrases.english: Since it is the highest of them all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה is named after the לולב because it is held highest.

steps.title: Then just raise the אתרוג higher
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה objects: if height is the reason, a person could lift the אתרוג above the לולב and say the ברכה on the אתרוג instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him raise the אתרוג higher and bless on it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges the answer by showing that a person could easily change which item is highest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule depended only on how high something is held, the ברכה would change with how a person holds his hands. That makes no sense for a fixed ברכה, so the answer cannot be just about physical position.

phrases.english: Then let him raise the etrog (higher) and bless (on it)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זריקא's reason that the לולב is the highest.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Height in the hand can be changed at will, so it cannot fix the wording of the ברכה.

steps.title: The palm tree is the tallest of the species
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא clarifies that he meant the palm tree, the source of the לולב, is naturally the tallest of all four plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: since in its species it is the highest of them all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זריקא explains what he really meant: not how high it is held, but how tall its kind of plant grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The palm tree grows far taller than a הדס bush, a ערבה, or an אתרוג tree. This height is built into nature and cannot be changed by how a person holds it, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: In its species (the kind of tree it grows on)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה is על נטילת לולב because the palm, the לולב's tree, is the tallest of the four species. This is a natural fact, not a matter of how one holds them.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since in its species it is the highest of them all.
phrases.notes: The palm tree is the tallest of the four plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by refining Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The answer seemed to mean that the לולב is held highest in the hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer means that the palm species is naturally the tallest, which cannot be changed.

steps.title: משנה: where in הלל the לולב is waved, according to בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה asks at which points in הלל the לולב is waved. בית הלל say: at הודו לה' at the start and end, and at אנא ה' הושיעה נא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה. And where would they wave? At 'Thank the Lord,' beginning and end, and at 'Please, Lord, save us.' This is the view of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, listing the points in הלל where people wave the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הודו לה' appears at the beginning and the end of the chapter in תהלים, so there are two waving points there, plus a third at הושיעה נא. This is בית הלל's list, and בית שמאי add to it next.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
'Thank the Lord': a verse in הלל
'Please, Lord, save us': a verse in הלל

phrases.english: Mishnah:
And where would they wave (the lulav)?
At 'Thank the Lord,' at the beginning and the end,
and at 'Please, Lord, save us';
these are the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; the earlier discussion of רבה's rulings is over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: wave at הודו לה' (beginning and end) and at אנא ה' הושיעה נא.

steps.title: בית שמאי add waving at הצליחה נא
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say one also waves at אנא ה' הצליחה נא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי say: also at 'Please, Lord, grant us success.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents the opposing view: בית שמאי add one more waving point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on בית הלל's list. The only disagreement is whether הצליחה נא, the second half of the same verse, also gets a waving.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Please grant success': second half of the verse

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai say:
Also at 'Please, Lord, grant us success.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to בית הלל in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: also wave at אנא ה' הצליחה נא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's eyewitness report
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא testifies that while everyone else waved, רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע waved only at אנא ה' הושיעה נא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I was watching רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע. All the people were waving their lulavim, but they waved only at 'Please, Lord, save us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא brings evidence from what he saw great sages actually do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast is within the verse אנא ה': everyone else also waved at הצליחה נא, but these two sages waved only at הושיעה נא. Their practice supports בית הלל against בית שמאי. It does not mean they skipped the waving at הודו לה'.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'only' in 'they waved only at הושיעה נא' is contrasted with הצליחה נא, the other half of the verse. It does not mean they skipped הודו לה'. The people were waving at הצליחה נא as well, like בית שמאי, but the sages did not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: צוֹפֶה הָיִיתִי בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: I was observing Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל הָעָם הָיוּ מְנַעְנְעִין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: that all the people were waving their lulavim,
and they did not wave
except at 'Please, Lord, save us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a report of actual practice into the מחלוקת of Steps 21–22.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's view that one does not wave at אנא ה' הצליחה נא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רבי עקיבא saw רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע do.

steps.title: Who mentioned waving at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה speaks of waving as if it were already known, when this משנה never introduced it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. Waving: who mentioned its name?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה opens with 'where do they wave' without first saying that waving is done at all. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the משנה's wording and flow. The word 'and' in 'and where' assumes something came before, so the גמרא asks what earlier source the משנה is building on.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא: start of the גמרא's discussion
Who mentioned it? (it was never introduced)

phrases.english: Gemara:
Waving: who mentioned it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the משנה of Step 21 is phrased.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opening words of the משנה, 'and where would they wave'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה assumes the reader knows about waving, yet waving was never introduced here.

steps.title: The משנה builds on an earlier משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an earlier משנה (on 29b) already mentioned waving, so this משנה simply continues from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands on (the משנה) there: any lulav that has three handbreadths, enough to wave with it, is valid. And now it says: where do they wave?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that waving was already mentioned in an earlier משנה, so it is fine for this משנה to take it for granted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה required a לולב to be three טפחים long so that it can be waved. That assumes waving is part of the מצוה. Our משנה now fills in the details of where in הלל the waving happens.

keyTerms.meaning: It is standing on (the source) there

steps.whatToRemember: Waving the לולב was established in the earlier משנה about its minimum size. This משנה adds where in הלל to wave: בית הלל at הודו and הושיעה נא, בית שמאי also at הצליחה נא.

phrases.english: It is standing on (the mishnah) there:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל לוּלָב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
phrases.english: Any lulav that has three handbreadths
enough to wave with it is valid,
and (now) it says: where do they wave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of Step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to assume waving without ever introducing it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Waving was introduced in the earlier משנה about a three-טפח לולב, and this משנה continues from it.

steps.title: How the שבועות loaves and lambs are waved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מנחות: the כהן places the שתי הלחם on the two lambs, puts his hand underneath, and waves them forward and back and up and down, based on the פסוק "אשר הונף ואשר הורם".
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: How are the two loaves and the two lambs of שבועות waved? He puts the two loaves on top of the two lambs, puts his hand under them, and waves them, moving them forward and back and lifting them up and down. This is because the פסוק says: "which is waved and which is lifted."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from מנחות that describes exactly how a waving is done. This prepares the next lines, which explain why the waving is done this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said the לולב is waved but never said how. This משנה about the שתי הלחם gives the pattern: forward and back, then up and down. The פסוק "הונף" (waved) and "הורם" (lifted) is the source for both kinds of movement.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about the קרבן on שבועות, not about the לולב. The גמרא brings it because it shows how waving is done, and the same kind of waving is used for the לולב.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
The two loaves and the two lambs of Shavuot,
how does he do (the waving)?

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁנֵי הַכְּבָשִׂין,
phrases.english: He places the two loaves on top of the two lambs,
and places his hand beneath them,
and waves, moving them forward and back,
raising and lowering.
phrases.notes: Two kinds of movement: sideways (forward and back) and vertical (up and down).

phrases.english: As it is stated: "Which is waved and which is lifted."
phrases.notes: שמות כט:כז. "Waved" points to forward and back. "Lifted" points to up and down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled that our משנה builds on an earlier mention of waving, the גמרא now brings a source showing how waving is actually done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waving of the שתי הלחם is done forward and back, then up and down, based on "אשר הונף ואשר הורם".

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the waving honors the Owner of the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that moving forward and back is for the One Who owns all four directions, and raising and lowering is for the One Who owns heaven and earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He moves them forward and back for the One Who owns the four directions. He raises and lowers them for the One Who owns heaven and earth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the meaning behind the two kinds of waving described in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each movement matches a part of the world. Sideways movement points to the four directions, and up and down points to heaven and earth. The message is that הקב"ה owns all of it, so the waving is a statement of His rule over the whole world.

keyTerms.meaning: The four directions (east, west, north, south)
To the One to Whom ... belongs

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא לְמִי שֶׁהָאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: He moves forward and back for the One Whose are the four directions,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה וּמוֹרִיד לְמִי שֶׁהַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: he raises and lowers for the One Whose are the heavens and the earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the movements the משנה described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waving shows that הקב"ה owns all four directions and heaven and earth.

steps.title: In the West: the waving holds back harmful winds and dews
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they taught a different reason in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: forward and back holds back harmful winds, and up and down holds back harmful dews.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they taught it like this: רבי חמא בר עוקבא said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: He moves them forward and back to stop harmful winds, and raises and lowers them to stop harmful dews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second explanation of the waving, from the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason is about praising הקב"ה. This reason is about protection: the waving is like a request to stop damage. Harmful winds come from the sides, so we wave to the sides, and harmful dews come from above, so we wave up and down.
steps.confusionAlert: Here "רוחות" means winds, not directions as in רבי יוחנן's line. The same word is used in a different sense.

phrases.english: In the West (Eretz Yisrael) they taught it this way:
Rabbi Chama bar Ukva said
that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא כְּדֵי לַעֲצוֹר רוּחוֹת רָעוֹת,
phrases.english: He moves forward and back in order to stop harmful winds,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה וּמוֹרִיד כְּדֵי לַעֲצוֹר טְלָלִים רָעִים.
phrases.english: he raises and lowers in order to stop harmful dews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from רבי יוחנן's for the same movements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waving serves to hold back harmful winds and harmful dews.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר אבין begins to draw a lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין (some say רבי יוסי בר זבידא) begins to draw a lesson from the waving with the words "זאת אומרת". The lesson itself continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said, and some say it was רבי יוסי בר זבידא: This teaches us...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. A new אמורא is about to draw a lesson from what was just taught, and the lesson comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "זאת אומרת" tells us that something new can be learned from the earlier statement. The גמרא is building on the idea that the waving holds back harm. The actual lesson is stated at the start of the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us; we learn from this

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not look for the lesson on this עמוד, because it continues on the next one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida:
This is to say (we learn from this):
phrases.notes: The lesson continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins drawing a lesson from the explanation that waving holds back harm.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An inference is introduced here, and its content follows on the next עמוד.
